Rashi on Eruvin 8b:10:1.english: That there is no more than ten on its diagonal - Because the mavoi is much shorter than it is wide, and its width combined with the four amot that extend to be added to it comes to no more than ten.

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:10:2.english: But its diagonal is more than ten - Thus its opening is wider than ten, since everything beneath the beam counts as the opening.

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:11:1.english: What is the law regarding using under the beam? - But it refers to alleyways (mevu'ot).

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:12:1.hebrew: קורה משום מחיצה - וחודו הפנימי יורד וסותם, הלכך אסור דמן המחיצה ולפנים בעי אשתמושי:
Rashi on Eruvin 8b:12:1.english: A beam [serves] as a partition - Its inner edge hangs down and closes off, therefore it is forbidden, because from the partition inward it requires use.

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:13:1.english: The Master holds it is a demarcation - For those from the inside we require it, and the inner side becomes a demarcation, and it is forbidden to make use from the demarcation outward:

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:13:2.english: From outside - That is, for the public domain, the outer side.

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:14:1.english: The Master holds that its inner edge descends and seals - Thus [the area] under the beam, from the partition outward, is forbidden.

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:15:1.hebrew: הכל מודים - במבוי שאין בו קורה, והכשירו בלחי שאסור להשתמש בין לחיים, כלומר כנגד הלחי, והאי דנקט בין לחיים אמבואות טובא קאי:
Rashi on Eruvin 8b:15:1.english: Everyone agrees - [This refers to] an alleyway that has no beam, but where they validated [it] with a jamb; it is forbidden to use [the space] between the jambs, i.e., opposite the jamb. The reason he said "between the jambs" refers to many alleyways.

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:16:1.hebrew: נעץ שתי יתידות - קביליי"ש נעוצות בכותל בעוביו שלצד רה"ר ונמצאת קורה שעליהן בולטת ונמשכת לחוץ יותר מן הכתלים וחודה הפנימי דבוק וסמוך לכותל: (*):(*)
Rashi on Eruvin 8b:16:1.english: He drove in two pegs - Pegs (Old French cheville) fixed into the thickness of the wall on the public-domain side, with a beam resting on them that projects outward beyond the walls, its inner edge attached and flush against the wall:

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:17:1.hebrew: לדברי האוסר - להשתמש תחת הקורה בכל מבואות, דטעמא משום חודו הפנימי יורד וסותם:
Rashi on Eruvin 8b:17:1.english: According to the one who forbids - [It is forbidden] to use under the beam in every mavoi, since the reason is that its inner edge descends and blocks [the opening].

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:17:2.hebrew: מתיר - כאן להשתמש במבוי הזה אגב הך קורה, שאינה על גבי מבוי, דכיון דחודו הפנימי סותם, נמצאת סתימת הקורה דבוקה לכתלים, וסתימה מעלייתא היא:
Rashi on Eruvin 8b:17:2.english: Permits - Here [it means] using this alleyway together with this beam that is not atop the alleyway, since its inner edge blocks [the opening], so the beam's blocking is attached to the walls, and it is a proper blocking.

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:17:3.hebrew: לדברי המתיר - להשתמש תחת הקורה אלמא חיצון יורד וסותם אוסר כל המבוי הזה עד שיביאו קורה אחרת, דאין הסתימה מחוברת לכתלים ויש אויר ביניהם, והכא לאו מחיצה ממש הוא, להכשיר הפסק אויר שמכאן ומכאן ע"י לבוד:
Rashi on Eruvin 8b:17:3.english: According to the one who permits - [it is permitted] to use under the beam. Evidently, an external beam that descends and blocks off the alley renders this entire alley forbidden until another beam is brought, because the blocking is not attached to the walls and there is air between them. [In the Gemara's case], however, it is not an actual partition; its purpose is to render permissible the gap of air on either side through lavud (notional contiguity).

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:1:1.english: But this is opposite that - It does not become a private-domain courtyard for Shabbat. Now we learn that it is opposite it, and even so it is permitted:

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:2:1.hebrew: ולרבה - דאמר לעיל אבל זה כנגד זה הוי מבוי מפולש ואסור (אפילו חצר), הא דרב, במאי מוקים לה? בזה שלא כנגד זה, ועל כרחיך כנגד דקאמר רב לאו דווקא, דהא אוקימנא טעמיה דרב בשלא עירבו, אבל עירבו אפילו מבוי מותר:
Rashi on Eruvin 8b:2:1.english: And for Rava - who said above that when the openings face each other it is a perforated alleyway and forbidden (even a courtyard). How does Rava establish that ruling of Rav? He establishes it in a case where the openings do not face each other. Of necessity, then, Rav's 'opposite each other' is not meant literally, since we have established Rav's reasoning as applying where they did not make an eruv; but if they did make an eruv, even a perforated alleyway is permitted:

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:2:2.hebrew: תרתי למה לי - הא תנא לה חצר שהרבים נכנסין לה בזו כו', ומילתיה דרב למשתרייה חצר מינה, מסתמא ואפילו זה כנגד זה, וכל שכן בזה שלא כנגד זה, ואיסור מבוי מאידך, מתניתין דחצר קטנה שמעינן:
Rashi on Eruvin 8b:2:2.english: Why do I need two? - The tanna already taught the case of a courtyard into which the public enters through this one, etc., and Rav's statement is needed to permit a courtyard by means of it. Presumably [it permits] even when the openings face each other, and all the more so when they do not face each other. And the prohibition of an alleyway from the other side, we learn from the mishna about a small courtyard:

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:3:1.english: If from there - From a courtyard into which the public enters, etc., which [the mishna] teaches is a private domain for Shabbat.

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:3:2.english: I would have thought - this, which is called a private domain (reshut hayachid).

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:3:3.hebrew: לזרוק - כלומר, מדאורייתא רה"י הוא, והזורק מרה"ר לתוכו חייב:
Rashi on Eruvin 8b:3:3.english: To throw - That is to say, by Torah law it is a private domain (reshut hayachid), and one who throws from the public domain (reshut harabim) into it is liable:

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:3:5.english: Say no - It is permitted, and [any prohibition here would be] only rabbinic; why would the Sages decree against it?

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:3:6.english: This teaches us - Rav [holds that it is] permitted.

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:4:1.hebrew: נדל - שרץ שיש לו רגלים הרבה, כדתניא בתורת כהנים (פרשת שמיני): מרבה רגלים זה נדל מבוי העשוי כנדל שפתוחין לו מבואות הרבה וראשיהן פתוחין לרשות הרבים וראשו פתוח לרשות הרבים אחר:
Rashi on Eruvin 8b:4:1.english: Nedal - A creature with many legs, as taught in Torat Kohanim (Parashat Shemini): 'One that multiplies legs' - this is the nedal, an alley constructed like a nedal, to which many alleys are open, with their heads open to the public domain, and its head open to the public domain [another].

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:4:2.hebrew: עושה צורת פתח לגדול - באחד משני ראשין, והאחרים קטנים, משתרו בלחי, וקורה בראשיהן על פני רשות הרבים:
Rashi on Eruvin 8b:4:2.english: He makes a doorway-shape for the large one - At one of its two ends. The others are small ones that are permitted with a lechi (a side post), and a beam on their tops spans the public domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:5:1.english: According to whom? According to Shmuel - who said that a crooked alleyway has the law of a closed one, since all these small alleyways are crooked. One enters by this route and exits by that route, and you say it does not require rectifying its crookedness, as Shmuel holds.

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:5:2.hebrew: ה"ג למה לי צורת פתח - אמאי אצרכת צורת פתח לגדול, הא איהו נמי אין פילושיו מכוונין:
Rashi on Eruvin 8b:5:2.english: Why do I need a doorway shape? - [The text reads:] Why do you require a doorway shape for the large one? For in its case too, its philosophical [i.e., geometric] reckonings are not exact.

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:5:3.hebrew: ועוד הא ההוא מבוי - דהוה באתריה דשמואל בנהרדעא וחשו ליה לדרב, כדאמר לעיל רמו עליה חומריה דרב וחומריה דשמואל:
Rashi on Eruvin 8b:5:3.english: Furthermore, this alley - This was in Shmuel's locale in Nehardea, and they were concerned for Rav's opinion, as stated above: they imposed upon it the stringency of Rav and the stringency of Shmuel:

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:6:1.english: He makes a doorway shape for all of them - the small ones:

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:6:2.english: From this side - [The walls are] curved toward the side of the large alleyway.

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:6:3.english: And on the other side - toward the public domain, it is permitted [i.e., the alley is valid] with a cheek-post or a beam.

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:7:1.english: One side is long - and its wall extends further into the public domain than the wall on the other side, like this: (*)

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:7:2.english: If less than four cubits - [If one side exceeds the other by only that much,] he places a beam diagonally across and uses the longer length here and the shorter length there:

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:7:3.english: Four cubits, one does not place a beam - on the top of the long wall, but rather one sets it back inward from its top, opposite the top of the short wall, and places it there:

Rashi on Eruvin 8b:8:1.hebrew: ובאלכסון לא הוי היכירא - שהרואה בני מבוי נמשכין ומשתמשין ברה"ר חוץ מכנגד כותל הקצר, אומר מותר להשתמש ברשות הרבים לפי שאין אותו העודף דומה שיהא מן המבוי:
Rashi on Eruvin 8b:8:1.english: And diagonally there would be no distinguishing mark - [The reason is that] one who sees the residents of the alley extending and using the public domain outside, except opposite the short wall, says it is permitted to use the public domain, since that excess does not look like it belongs to the alley:

Tosafot on Eruvin 8b:15:1.hebrew: הכל מודים בבין לחיים דאסור - טעמא משום דלחי הוי אפילו משהו, ואתי לאפוקי. אבל בקורה דרחבה טפח ליכא למיחש. אבל אין לפרש דטעמא דרב חסדא משום דסבר קורה משום היכר, ולחי משום מחיצה, ומשום היכר; ובין לחיים אסור, ואינו יכול להשתמש אלא מן המחיצה שלפנים, דהא אביי אית ליה לעיל (עירובין ד' ה.) גבי היה גבוה מכ' ובא למעטו. לחד לישנא, קורה משום מחיצה, וכ"ש לחי. וקא אמר בסמוך: מסתברא מילתיה דר' יוחנן, תחת הקורה אבל בין לחיים אסור. ורבא נמי אית ליה בפירקין דתרוייהו משום היכירא, ובסמוך מודה רבא דאסור להשתמש בין לחיים היכא דרחב ארבעה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 8b:15:1.english: All agree that the space between the cheeks is forbidden - The reason is that a cheek counts even if it is something small, and one may come to remove it. But with a beam that is a handbreadth wide there is no concern. But one should not explain that the reason of Rav Chisda is that he holds a beam serves as a sign (hekker) and a cheek as a partition, and also as a sign; and between the cheeks it is forbidden, and one may use [the space] only from the partition on the inner side. For Abaye holds above (Eruvin 5a), regarding [a partition] higher than twenty, that he came to exclude it. According to one version, a beam [counts] as a partition, and certainly a cheek. And he says below that the statement of R. Yochanan is reasonable: under the beam [it is permitted], but between the cheeks it is forbidden. And Rava too holds in this chapter that both are a matter of sign, and below Rava concedes that it is forbidden to use the space between the cheeks where it is four wide.

Tosafot on Eruvin 8b:4:1.english: An alley made like a nedal - Rabbeinu Tam explains: small alleys open onto a large alley from two sides, but they are not opposite one another. If they were, the alley would be pierced through (mefulash). This is like the legs of a nedal, which has two rows of legs, one on the right and one on the left, and they are not opposite one another.

Tosafot on Eruvin 8b:5:1.hebrew: והא ההוא מבוי עקום דהוה בנהרדע' ורמו עליה חומריה דרב - ממאי דחשו נמי לדשמואל, לא פריך ויצטרך דלתות; דהא דחשו משום דנהרדעא אתריה דשמואל הוה, אבל מדחשו לדרב באתריה דשמואל, פריך שפיר:
Tosafot on Eruvin 8b:5:1.english: But that crooked alley in Nehardea, upon which Rav's stringency was applied - How do we know that they were also concerned for Shmuel's [view], such that [the Gemara] would not raise the objection and [Shmuel] would need doors? [The answer is that] they were concerned about it because Nehardea was Shmuel's place; but since they were concerned for Rav's [view] in Shmuel's place, the objection is valid.

Tosafot on Eruvin 8b:7:1.hebrew: מניח את הקורה באלכסון - פ"ה משתמש כאן בארוכה וכאן בקצרה, והדין עמו שפי' כן; דאי לא תימא הכי, אמאי מניח את הקורה באלכסון? הא בעינן קורה לכל הפחות דבוקה במבוי, כדאמר בסמוך גבי ב' יתידות בשני כותלים כו'. לדברי המתיר אסור, ואף על פי שכאן מונח ראשו האחד על גבי המבוי, אין סברא לחלק. וא"ת, והיכי שרי להשתמש נגד הארוך? הא אין כאן אלא ב' מחיצות? וי"ל, דאית ליה קורה משום מחיצה, ומאן דאית ליה משום מחיצה הוי אפילו דאורייתא, כדמוכח בפירקין. אי נמי, כיון דצידו האחד ארוך, מסתמא לא בקעי בה רבים, ולא גזרו ביה רבנן הואיל ובטל לגבי מבוי, אע"ג דאית ביה ד' על ד':
Tosafot on Eruvin 8b:7:1.english: Places the beam diagonally - Rashi's commentary (Peirush HaKuntres) uses the long [beam] here and the short [beam] there, and the reasoning is with him, for he explains it this way. For if you do not say so, why does he place the beam diagonally? We require a beam that is at least attached to the alleyway (mavoi), as is stated below regarding two pegs on two walls, etc. According to the one who permits it, it is forbidden. And although here one end rests on the alleyway, there is no logic to distinguish. And if you ask, how is it permitted to use [the beam] opposite the long [side]? Here there are only two partitions! One can answer that he holds a beam serves as a partition (mechitza), and according to the one who holds it serves as a partition, it is even d'Oraita, as is evident in this chapter. Alternatively, since one of its sides is long, presumably people do not breach through it, and the Rabbis did not decree regarding it, since it is nullified with respect to the alleyway, even though it has four by four [cubits].
